h1: Strong beer ABV and how fast the alcohol adds up
title: Strong Beer ABV and How Fast It Adds Up | Craft Beer School
desc: What strong beer means on an Indian label, how ABV ranges differ by style and how fast the alcohol in a few strong beers adds up.
teaser: An 8% beer is not a little stronger than a 4% beer. It is twice as strong. Here is what that means over an evening.
standfirst: A few percentage points on a label look small. In the glass they double the alcohol. This guide explains what strong beer means in India and in craft styles, shows how an evening adds up and how to taste strength before it surprises you.
sections: Double the ABV, double the alcohol

ABV is a share of the glass. A 500 ml beer at 4% holds 20 ml of pure alcohol. The same glass at 8% holds 40 ml. That is twice as much, not a little more. People tend to read 8% as "slightly stronger" than 5% because the numbers are close together. The alcohol in the glass is 60% higher.

Brewers get a higher ABV by starting with more sugar in the wort. More malt means more fermentable sugar, which the yeast turns into more alcohol. Our guide to calculating ABV shows the sum brewers use.
What strong means on an Indian label

In India the word strong on a beer label usually means a lager above about 5% ABV. Most strong beers sit somewhere between 5 and 8%. They are commonly sold in 650 ml bottles and 500 ml cans. Excise categories and the exact cut-offs vary by state, so the same beer can be labelled and taxed differently across borders. Check the ABV printed on the label rather than trusting the word strong.

A single 650 ml bottle at 8% holds 52 ml of pure alcohol. That is about 5.2 UK units, roughly the same as four small 30 ml pegs of whisky at 42.8%. It is easy to drink one of those bottles in the time it takes to drink one peg.

Craft beer covers a much wider range than the supermarket shelf. Rough, typical ranges look like this:

  • Light lager, Berliner weisse, many sours: 3 to 4.5%
  • Pilsner, wheat beer, pale ale: 4.5 to 5.5%
  • IPA: 5.5 to 7.5%
  • Double IPA, Belgian Tripel: 7.5 to 10%
  • Imperial stout, barleywine: 8 to 12% and sometimes more

A brewpub menu can put a 4% session beer and a 10% imperial stout next to each other at the same price. Read the ABV column before you order, not after.

Here is a realistic brewpub evening, worked out so you can check it:

  • One 400 ml wheat beer at 5%: 20 ml
  • One 400 ml IPA at 6.5%: 26 ml
  • One 400 ml double IPA at 8.5%: 34 ml
  • One 250 ml imperial stout at 10%: 25 ml

That is 105 ml of pure alcohol, about 10.5 UK units, from four drinks that did not feel like much. The liver clears roughly one unit an hour, so most of that is still in your blood as you leave. Swap the double IPA and the stout for two 400 ml session beers at 4% and the total drops to 78 ml. That is about a quarter less alcohol for the same four rounds and the same evening out.
You can taste strength if you look for it

Alcohol has a flavour and a feel. It shows up as warmth in the throat and chest, a slight sweetness and a fuller body. In a well made strong beer it is smooth and folded into the malt. In a badly made one, often fermented too warm, it tastes hot and solvent-like. Our guide to solvent and hot alcohol notes explains that fault.

Learning to notice warmth helps you pace yourself. If a beer feels warming after two sips, treat it as a sipping beer. That is why good bars serve imperial stouts and barleywines in 200 to 250 ml measures.

Strong beers are meant to be sipped, warmed slightly and enjoyed slowly. Served at 10 to 13 °C rather than ice cold, they show more aroma, which makes a small glass more satisfying. Our guide to tasting strong beers covers glassware and temperature.

Pair the strong one with food and water. Split a bottle between two or three people. Order it last, when your palate has done its main work, rather than first. You will get more flavour from the beer and much less alcohol from the night.
Check the ABV of your favourite

Look up the ABV of the beer you drink most often. Multiply it by your usual pour size and divide by 100 to get millilitres of alcohol. If the number surprises you, try a lower strength beer of the same style next time and see whether you miss anything.
faqs: What ABV counts as strong beer in India?
Strong beer on Indian labels usually means lager above about 5% ABV, most often between 5 and 8%. Exact categories vary by state.
How much alcohol is in a 650 ml bottle of strong beer?
At 8% ABV it holds 52 ml of pure alcohol, about 5.2 UK units.
Why are strong beers served in smaller glasses?
They carry more alcohol per millilitre and are meant to be sipped. A 200 to 250 ml pour lets you enjoy the flavour without the alcohol of a full pint.
Can you taste the alcohol in strong beer?
Yes. Alcohol shows as warmth, slight sweetness and fuller body. A hot, solvent taste usually points to a fermentation fault.
